## About this guide

Use this guide to identify expected fields and locate their cells in a form.

The Terminology guide defines the concepts used here.

Install `ros.form.model` using the instructions on the home page. This package supplies definitions, not blank Excel forms.

## Choose the gear and version

Read the version from the submitted form or its accompanying documentation before choosing the model.

Use `ROS_FORM_LL` for longline or `ROS_FORM_PS` for purse seine. Versions 3.3.0, 4.0.0, 4.1.0 and 4.2.0 are distinct.

```{r}
library(ros.form.model)
# List the supported form identifiers.
ROS_FORMS
# List the supported form versions.
ROS_FORM_VERSIONS
# Load the explicitly selected form model.
form_model_definition <- ros_form(name = ROS_FORM_LL, version = ROS_FORM_VERSION_3_3_0)
```

If the version is unclear, ask the provider to confirm it before validating the form.

## Find a sheet and its fields

```{r}
# List the sheets in form model order.
names(form.model::form_sheets(form_model_definition))
# Inspect the metadata sheet layout.
form.model::form_layout(form_model_definition, id = "META")
# Read the metadata field definitions.
form_model_fields <- form.model::form_fields(form_model_definition, sheet = "META")
# List the sheets in form model order.
names(form_model_fields)
# Inspect the first metadata field.
form_model_fields[[1L]]
```

The sheet list follows model order. Field definitions show their name, type, mandatory flag and coordinates.

Field identifiers combine the exact sheet name and field name: `<sheet>.<field>`.

Cell layouts declare fixed coordinates. Table fields follow column order; the layout gives the starting row.

## Inspect primary keys

Table sheets declare ordered primary keys using the field names of each supported version.

```{r}
# Inspect the fields that identify a record.
form.model::form_sheets(form_model_definition)[["E-SET-CATCHES"]]$primary_key
```

The declarations identify rows within each sheet of a submitted form:

- `V-TRIP`: trip.
- `E-SET`: trip and set.
- `E-SET-CATCHES`: trip, set and catch.
- Both specimen sheets: trip, set, catch and specimen.
- Tag details: trip, set, catch and specimen.
- LL 3.3.0 branchline configurations: trip, configuration and section.
- Hooks: trip, set and hook type.
- Baits: trip, set, species and condition.
- Lights: trip, set, light type and colour.
- PS branchlines: trip, set and configuration.
- Surface or daily activities: trip and activity datetime.

Version 3.3.0 uses the corresponding `*_number` fields; versions 4.0.0 and 4.1.0 use `*_id` fields.

These entries apply where the corresponding sheet exists; inspect `primary_key` for its exact field names.

These are model declarations; submitted-data checks must be implemented by `form.validation`.

## Optional keys and row information

LL hauling biteoffs use `unique_key` in versions 3.3.0, 4.0.0, 4.1.0 and 4.2.0.
LL branchline configurations use it in versions 4.0.0, 4.1.0 and 4.2.0.
These sheets retain their parent keys and do not declare primary keys.

```{r}
# Load the explicitly selected form model.
biteoff_form_model <- ros_form(name = ROS_FORM_LL, version = ROS_FORM_VERSION_4_0_0)
# Select the hauling biteoff sheet definition.
biteoff_sheet_definition <- form.model::form_sheets(biteoff_form_model)[["E-SET-HAULING-BITEOFFS"]]
# Inspect the link to the parent sheet.
biteoff_sheet_definition$parent_key
# Inspect the optional record key.
biteoff_sheet_definition$unique_key
# Inspect the row information requirement.
biteoff_sheet_definition$at_least_one
```

A complete trip/set/configuration combination must be unique within the biteoff sheet.
Missing configurations remain allowed. Different configurations may belong to the same set.

For biteoffs, `at_least_one` warns when a populated row supplies neither configuration nor biteoff count.
For branchline configurations, it warns when only the trip identifier is supplied.
A count of zero is supplied information. Entirely empty rows do not trigger this check.
Parent-key and mandatory-field errors remain separate from these warnings.

## Locate a field from a report

```{r}
# Select the liaison officer field.
form_model_field <- form_model_fields[["META.liaison_officer_full_name"]]
# Read the physical row number.
form_model_field$row
# Read the physical column number.
form_model_field$column
# Inspect the required-value setting.
form_model_field$mandatory
```

Row and column numbers are one-based: column 1 is A, column 5 is E.

Use these coordinates to inspect the original Excel form. Loading a definition does not change that form.

A field may also declare allowed values or a reference list. Reference contents are supplied during validation.

Continue with [ros.form.validation](https://ultreia-io.github.io/ros.form.validation/) to check a submitted form.

## Download a form model

```{r, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# Show website downloads or the corresponding installed resource.
if (identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true")) {
  # Link to the unchanged LL and PS YAML definitions copied into the website.
  cat("* [LL 4.2.0 form model](../models/4.2.0/ll-form.yaml)\n",
      "* [PS 4.2.0 form model](../models/4.2.0/ps-form.yaml)\n", sep = "")
} else {
  # Identify the installed directory containing the same definitions.
  cat("The form models are installed under `system.file(\"models\", package = \"ros.form.model\")`.\n")
}
```
